      <title>The Foreigner's Bow, the Serpent's Tongue, and the Eyes of a Goat</title>
      <description>When Krishna Deva Raya's three-month siege of Raichur stalls, a Portuguese horse trader named Christovao de Figueiredo asks permission to walk down to the wall with twenty musketeers — and ends the siege in days, picking off defenders until the city's captain leans through an embrasure and is shot dead through the forehead. The king bows his head to Figueiredo before his entire army. Then Asad Khan slips into court as ambassador and weaves a web of lies that convinces Krishna to behead the brave prisoner Salabat Khan; the king's six-year-old son and heir is poisoned by the minister's own boy; and Krishna, dying, drags the man who once saved his life by sacrificing a goat — Saluva Timma — to the place of executions and tears out his eyes. Based on A Forgotten Empire (Vijayanagara) by Robert Sewell (1900).</description>
